analysis.title: "The Age Of Idiosyncratic Risk": BofA Says Options Are Underpricing Megacap Earnings Blowups, While Europe Overpays
key_insights: BofA's Global Equity Volatility Insights note (team led by Benjamin Bowler) finds single-stock fragility remains a defining feature of equity markets into year-end, even with index vol subdued.
3-month ATM weighted-average stock vol is 38% for the SPX Top 50, about 2.5x the equivalent index vol, and 31% in Europe, about 1.8x the SX5E.

BofA's conclusion is that US earnings vol is still cheap and European earnings vol is rich. The US earnings vol premium has risen, but realised moves have risen more, with the underpricing most pronounced in megacaps.
Europe shows the opposite pattern: implied earnings risk is near historical extremes, yet only about a third of stocks have recently moved more than options implied.

BofA defines 'fragility events' as days when a stock moves more than 3 sigma relative to its trailing 21-day vol. Last year set a record in Europe and 2026 is tracking close pro-rata, on course for one of Europe's top five years.

BofA measures earnings pricing by comparing 'excess' implied vol around each earnings date (the expiry containing the release versus an interpolated no-earnings fair value) with the excess vol that subsequently realises.
For the equal-weighted SPX Top 50, the implied earnings premium is at its 85th percentile and the realised premium is at its 91st.

Market-cap weighting widens the US gap: realised earnings vol for the index-weighted SPX Top 50 is at its 100th percentile versus the 77th for implied, so the bigger the company, the bigger the underpricing.

The US implied earnings premium has grown in absolute vol points (85th percentile) but not as a share of total stock variance (51st percentile). Options are pricing more earnings risk mostly because they price more risk overall.
More than half of SPX Top 50 names by count, and more than two-thirds by market cap, have recently realised bigger earnings moves than options implied. The weighted reading is in its 98th percentile.
In August BofA flagged that all six Mag7 stocks that had reported realised moves far greater than implied, a first in the ChatGPT era. The options market has not caught up since.

In Europe, excess vol priced around earnings is at its 94th percentile for equal-weighted SX5E names, while realised is at the 78th. Index-weighted, implied is at the 94th percentile and realised at the 72nd, so the richness is not a function of company size.
Normalised for stock vol level, European earnings risk as a share of total variance is at its 74th percentile.
Only about a third of European stocks, and a similarly low share by market cap, have recently moved more on earnings than options anticipated, a 33rd percentile reading on both measures.
BofA's trade conclusion: own US single-stock earnings optionality, particularly in megacaps where underpricing is most extreme, and sell (or be a very reluctant buyer of) European earnings vol.
earnings_insights: US megacap earnings season: BofA says options underprice realised earnings moves, with the index-weighted SPX Top 50 realised earnings vol at its 100th percentile versus 77th for implied.
More than half of SPX Top 50 names by count and more than two-thirds by market cap have recently realised bigger earnings moves than implied (98th percentile weighted reading).
European earnings: implied excess vol at its 94th percentile for equal-weighted SX5E names versus realised at the 78th. Only about a third of European stocks recently moved more than implied.

trade_ideas.description: Own US single-stock earnings optionality, particularly in megacaps, over reporting season
trade_ideas.rationale: Realised earnings moves have outrun implied, with the index-weighted SPX Top 50 realised earnings vol at the 100th percentile versus 77th for implied.

trade_ideas.description: Sell, or be a very reluctant buyer of, European single-stock earnings vol
trade_ideas.rationale: Implied excess earnings vol is at the 94th percentile while only about a third of stocks have moved more than implied.

risk_factors: Megacap earnings could again produce realised moves well above implied, as with all six reporting Mag7 stocks in August.
AI capex, hyperscaler guidance and the debt financing it landing on the same few earnings calls could stress-test the underpricing.
Index calm masks single-stock fragility: the index is a few points from a record while one in six members is in a 50%+ drawdown.
For options sellers, idiosyncratic risk can arrive for many names at once.

US implied earnings premium (equal-weighted SPX Top 50) at the 85th percentile versus realised at the 91st. Index-weighted: implied 77th, realised 100th.

Europe: implied excess earnings vol at the 94th percentile (equal-weighted SX5E) versus realised at the 78th. Index-weighted: implied 94th, realised 72nd. Earnings risk as a share of total variance is at the 74th percentile.
Share of stocks recently moving more than implied on earnings: US weighted reading at the 98th percentile, Europe at the 33rd percentile.
Trade expression: long US single-stock earnings optionality (especially megacaps), short or avoid European earnings vol.
